subject: maths
question: I bought two speakers for ₹1,200. I sold the first one at a loss of 8% and the second at a gain of 22%. If, on the whole I made neither a loss nor a gain, find the cost price (in ₹) of the first speaker.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

By the rule of alligation, if the overall transaction results in neither loss nor gain (0%), the ratio of their cost prices is inversely proportional to their respective percentage changes.

Ratio of CP₁ : CP₂ = Gain% : Loss% = 22 : 8 = 11 : 4.

Total ratio parts = 11 + 4 = 15 parts.

Value of 15 parts = ₹1200 ⇒ 1 part = ₹80.

CP of the first speaker (11 parts) = 11 × 80 = ₹880.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹880.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Total Cost Price (CP) of two speakers = ₹1,200

Loss on the first speaker = 8%

Gain on the second speaker = 22%

Overall transaction result = No profit, no loss (0%)

**Formula Used:**

In a case of no profit and no loss, Absolute Loss on one item = Absolute Gain on the other item.
